prompt.context_jp: 新島家からのバーベキューの招待状が届いてから、白石の家には気詰まりな静けさが続いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 新島家からのバーベキューの招待状___届いてから、白石の家には気詰まりな静けさが続いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this opening line.

feedback.correct_en: The invitation is brand-new information introducing the whole scene — が marks this freshly-arriving event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the invitation as already-known topic, which clashes with 届いてから reporting its arrival. を doesn't fit — 届く is intransitive here.

contrast_examples.en: That letter — I threw it away. (already known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 台所に立つ母の背中は狭く、万理華は言葉を選びかねてただ包丁の音に耳を澄ませていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 台所に立つ母の背中___狭く、万理華は言葉を選びかねて…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that frames the mother's back as the described theme.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator sets 母の背中 as the topic and comments on it (狭く). は carries the characterizing comment naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the back as new information, which doesn't match this reflective description. に is locative, wrong here.

contrast_examples.jp: 母の背中は小さかった。
contrast_examples.en: Her mother's back was small. (comment on topic)

prompt.context_jp: 母娘の間に落ちた沈黙が、まな板の音を妙にはっきりと響かせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母娘の間に落ちた沈黙___、まな板の音を妙にはっきりと響かせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The silence is newly introduced as the agent that caused the knife-sound to stand out. が marks this emerging subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the silence a known topic, but it's just appeared here. で doesn't fit this subject role.

prompt.context_jp: 母の返事は思いのほか穏やかで、万理華は思わず息をついた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母の返事___思いのほか穏やかで、万理華は思わず息をついた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The reply has just occurred and is now being commented on as a theme (穏やかで). は fits the characterizing comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the reply as a sudden new event, but the sentence is reflecting on its quality. も implies 'also' which doesn't fit.

prompt.context_jp: 青い煙がまとまらずに漂うばかりで、鉄板の熱はいっこうに上がらない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 青い煙___まとまらずに漂うばかりで、鉄板の熱はいっこうに上がらない。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The blue smoke is being newly observed on scene — が marks the perceived subject. Note the contrast later: 鉄板の熱は… (known contrastive topic).
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the smoke as an established topic, but it's being noticed here. を doesn't match 漂う (intransitive).

prompt.context_jp: そこへ、いかにも慣れた足取りで一人の女性が石段を登ってきて、状況を一目で見て取った。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこへ、いかにも慣れた足取りで一人の女性___石段を登ってきて…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that introduces this new character.

feedback.correct_en: A completely new character enters the scene — 一人の女性 is unidentified and newly perceived, so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose she's an already-known topic, which she isn't. に marks direction/goal, not the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 一人の女性が入ってきた。
その女性は看護師だった。

prompt.context_jp: 火はいつしか勢いよく燃え上がり、鉄板の上ではソーセージや野菜が音を立て始めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 火___いつしか勢いよく燃え上がり、鉄板の上では…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The fire was already in focus in earlier scenes (struggling to light). Now it's taken up again as topic — は signals topic continuation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce the fire as if newly discovered, but we've been watching it the whole time. も would mean 'also fire', which doesn't fit.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介の目には、遠くで談笑する娘の姿がいつになく柔らかく映った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 圭介の目には、遠くで談笑する娘の姿___いつになく柔らかく映った。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is a perception sentence (映る). The daughter's figure appears to him as a freshly noticed sight — が marks what he perceives.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn her figure into an established topic, losing the sense of fresh perception.

contrast_examples.en: Stars are visible at night. (general comment)

prompt.context_jp: 母が口にした「楽しかった」という一言は、いかにも軽く発せられたが、その重さを万理華だけは知っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: …その重さを万理華だけ___知っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle after 万理華だけ.

feedback.correct_en: 万理華だけは carries a strong contrastive sense: 'Mariha alone (as opposed to the others) knew'. は after だけ highlights exclusivity-by-contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as flat identification, losing the 'only she, no one else' nuance. を is already used for 重さ.

contrast_examples.en: He was the one who knew. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 母の声はいつになく素直だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母の声___いつになく素直だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is a characterizing comment about the mother's voice (a known participant). は marks the topic being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn this into a sudden-discovery exclamation; the sentence is a quiet reflective observation.

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣は湯気を立てる皿から目を上げ、幼馴染の言葉を意外そうに受け止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 麻衣___湯気を立てる皿から目を上げ、幼馴染の言葉を意外そうに受け止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Mai is an established character, and the sentence tracks what she did next. は marks the ongoing topic/agent for multi-verb narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would freshly introduce her or spotlight 'it was Mai who…', not fitting this smooth narrative flow.

contrast_examples.en: She was the one who looked up. (focus/new)

prompt.context_jp: 風が銀杏を揺らし、光の粒がテーブルの上に散った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 風が銀杏___揺らし、光の粒がテーブルの上に散った。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 揺らす is transitive — the wind shakes the ginkgo. を marks 銀杏 as the direct object of that action.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would create two subjects. に would mark a destination, which doesn't match 'shake something'.

prompt.context_jp: 熱を確かめようと圭介は網に手を近づけ、慌てて指を引っ込めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 熱を確かめようと圭介は網___手を近づけ、慌てて指を引っ込めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 近づける takes に to mark the target you're moving something toward. He moves his hand toward the grill.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an action, not a destination. を doesn't mark a target with 近づける.

contrast_examples.jp: 口にマイクを近づける。
contrast_examples.en: Bring the mic close to one's mouth.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介は歩幅を合わせ、少し遅れて彼女の隣に並んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 圭介は歩幅___合わせ、少し遅れて彼女の隣に並んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 歩幅を合わせる is a set collocation — 合わせる is transitive and takes を on the thing being matched/adjusted.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would be used for the thing you're matching TO (e.g. 相手に合わせる). が doesn't mark the object of a transitive verb.

prompt.context_jp: うち 姉が ずっと入院してて 両親が付きっきりだったから
prompt.prompt_jp: うち 姉___ずっと入院してて 両親が付きっきりだったから
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle Moriya uses when revealing new personal info.

feedback.correct_en: Moriya is introducing her sister as new background information in a subordinate explanation. が fits new-info/subject in a reason clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would suggest the sister is already a known topic between them; here Moriya is first mentioning her.

contrast_examples.en: My sister was in hospital… (introducing info)
My sister is well. (comment on known person)

prompt.context_jp: 彼女は腕まくりをして、火のつかない炭の山に近づいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女は腕まくり___して、火のつかない炭の山に近づいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 腕まくりをする is a set 'noun+をする' pattern — the activity-noun takes を as the object of する.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a means. に would mark a target. Neither works with the suru-nominal pattern here.

prompt.context_jp: 新島家の面々と友利が集まり、テーブルの脇では圭介がしゃがみ込んで火をおこそうと悪戦苦闘していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: …圭介がしゃがみ込んで火をおこそうと___していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures Keisuke's hard struggle with the fire?

feedback.correct_en: 悪戦苦闘 means 'a bitter uphill fight' — the right flavor for struggling to light a fire that won't catch.
feedback.incorrect_en: 右往左往 means running around in confusion (not just one task). 一心不乱 means wholeheartedly focused — too positive here.

prompt.context_jp: 蓮司は皿を差し出そうとして、その相手の風格に一瞬たじろいだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蓮司は皿を差し出そうとして、その相手の___に一瞬たじろいだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word describes the imposing aura that made Renji flinch?

feedback.correct_en: 風格 is 'dignified presence / commanding air' — exactly what intimidates Renji about the older woman.
feedback.incorrect_en: 風景 is 'scenery'. 風習 is 'custom'. Neither describes a person's bearing.

prompt.context_jp: 部長が昔の恩を思い出し、便宜を図る形で話をまとめてくれたらしいことは、圭介の胸に静かに沁みていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部長が昔の恩を思い出し、___を図る形で話をまとめてくれたらしい…
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits — 'arranging matters as a favor'?

feedback.correct_en: 便宜を図る is a fixed business-register phrase meaning 'extend a courtesy/accommodation'. It fits the boss doing a favor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 便利 means 'convenient' as an adjective — it doesn't collocate with 図る. 都合をつける exists but 都合を図る does not.

contrast_examples.jp: 便宜を図っていただく。

prompt.context_jp: 短い時間だったが、家族の輪に彼女がいてくれた温もりが確かにあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 短い時間だったが、家族の___に彼女がいてくれた温もりが確かにあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word describes the circle of family she joined?

feedback.correct_en: 家族の輪 is the standard idiom for 'the family circle' — the warm group gathered together.
feedback.incorrect_en: 環 is more technical ('ring/cycle'). 円 is a geometric circle/yen, not used for human groups.

prompt.context_jp: いいんですよ グチャグチャで こういうときはね どんどん ぶっちゃけちゃったほうが すっきりしますから
prompt.prompt_jp: こういうときはね どんどん ___ちゃったほうが すっきりしますから
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke tells Moriya to just let it all out — pick the casual verb.

feedback.correct_en: ぶっちゃける is casual slang for 'spill it, be blunt'. It matches Keisuke's warm, informal tone of comforting her.
feedback.incorrect_en: 打ち明ける is more formal/earnest ('confess'). 言い放つ means to declare harshly — the opposite feeling.

prompt.context_jp: 新島さん 部長に掛け合ってくれたんだって 守屋さんの企画 いい企画だから もったいないって
prompt.prompt_jp: 新島さん 部長に___くれたんだって 守屋さんの企画 いい企画だから もったいないって
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits — 'negotiated with the boss on your behalf'?

feedback.correct_en: 掛け合う means to negotiate / plead on someone's behalf — a workplace idiom fitting Niijima arguing to save the project.
feedback.incorrect_en: 問い合わせる is just 'to inquire' (information). 言い合う means 'argue/quarrel', wrong tone.

prompt.context_jp: 頬に赤みを差した幼い顔には、いかなる大人にも真似できない一途さがあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頬に赤みを差した幼い顔には、いかなる大人にも真似できない___があった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures Mariha's childlike single-mindedness here?

feedback.correct_en: 一途さ means 'devoted, single-minded earnestness' — the quality a child has that adults can't fake.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一体感 is 'sense of unity' (group feeling). 一瞬 is 'a moment' (noun of time), not a quality.

prompt.context_jp: あの手際のよさ 絶妙な火おこし
prompt.prompt_jp: あの___のよさ 絶妙な火おこし
prompt.prompt_en: What's being praised about her fire-starting?

feedback.correct_en: 手際のよさ = 'skillfulness / deftness'. It's the standard phrase for praising someone's smooth technique.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手間 is 'trouble/time required' (negative framing). 手順 is 'procedure' — neutral, doesn't take よさ idiomatically.

contrast_examples.en: It takes a lot of effort.

prompt.context_jp: 忘れかけていた郷里の冬の匂いが、鼻の奥に蘇ってくるようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 忘れかけていた郷里の冬の匂いが、鼻の奥に___くるようだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits — the scent coming back vividly?

feedback.correct_en: 蘇る means 'be revived / come back to life' — perfect for a long-forgotten sensory memory welling up.
feedback.incorrect_en: 思い出す is for actively recalling (a person remembers); it doesn't take 匂いが as subject this way. 返る doesn't fit for memories/scents.

prompt.context_jp: 守屋 confesses to Niijima on the night walk.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds the most natural for Moriya's hesitant confession?

choices.text: 新島さんのこと 好きなんだと思います
新島さんのことを好きと思います
新島さんが好きと思っています

feedback.correct_en: The real line uses こと to soften the topic + 〜んだと思います for a tentative, honest tone. This matches her hesitant, drunk-ish confession.
feedback.incorrect_en: B drops the explanatory ん and sounds flat/translated. C combines 〜と思っています awkwardly; speakers don't normally announce ongoing feelings this stiffly.

contrast_examples.jp: 好きなんだと思います。

prompt.context_jp: Moriya thanks Niijima for pleading her case.
prompt.prompt_en: Which thank-you sounds most natural in this workplace-polite register?

choices.text: 部長に掛け合ってくださったって 聞きました。ありがとうございました
部長に掛け合ってもらったって 聞きました。ありがとう
部長に掛け合ったと聞きました。感謝します

feedback.correct_en: 〜てくださる honors the person who did the favor, and ありがとうございました closes it politely — the right register for a colleague-to-senior thanks.
feedback.incorrect_en: B drops the honorific (〜てもらう is neutral) and uses casual ありがとう — too flat. C uses stiff 感謝します, which sounds written/formal in speech.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けてくださってありがとうございました。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you for kindly helping me.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けてくれてありがとう。

prompt.context_jp: Mariha hands her mother warm cocoa.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for the child-form offering warm cocoa?

choices.text: 冷えてきましたね 温まりますよ
冷えてきますね 温まるでしょう
寒くなってます 温めますよ

feedback.correct_en: 冷えてきましたね uses 〜てきた to mark 'has been getting cold', with the shared-feeling ね. 温まりますよ (intransitive) correctly says 'this will warm you'.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses non-past 冷えてきます which sounds like a weather forecast, not a present comment. C's 温めます is transitive ('I'll heat something'), wrong for 'you'll warm up'.

prompt.context_jp: Moriya tells Niijima that warm people naturally gather around him.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is the most natural way to say 'such people naturally gather around you'?

choices.text: 自然と そういう人が 集まってくるんでしょうね
自然に そういう人を 集めるんでしょうね
自然に そういう人が 集まるでしょうね

feedback.correct_en: 自然と + intransitive 集まってくる + んでしょうね gives the soft, inferring 'they just naturally come together around you' — matches her gentle observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: B switches to transitive 集める ('you gather them'), which implies he's actively recruiting. C drops 〜てくる and んです, losing the warm inferential tone.
